Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:59: The fifth aspect concerning honor is what the prophet says (Isaiah 43:7) "all that is called by My Name, and for My glory I have created it," etc., and they say in the midrash (Yalkut Yeshayahu, remez 252), on this verse - their words: "and can it be that a person should be called by the Omnipresent's own name? Rather, the Omnipresent is called Merciful, as it is said (Psalms 103:8) 'the Lord is merciful and gracious' - you too be merciful, and do gratuitous kindness. The Omnipresent is called Righteous, as it is said (ibid. 145:17) 'the Lord is righteous in all His ways' - you too be righteous. He is called Pious, as it is said 'and pious in all His works' - you too be pious; therefore it is said 'all that is called by My Name,' and it says (Joel 3:5) 'whoever calls upon the Name of the Lord shall be saved,' and it says (Proverbs 16:4) 'the Lord has made everything for its purpose'" - so far. Along this line, which our Sages, of blessed memory, explain in "all that is called by My Name," "and for My glory I have created it" is understood, this being the honor of the Holy One, blessed be He - that people do His will and His deeds so that they are truly called by His Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:60: The words of the Zohar (Terumah 155a) agree with this interpretation - his words: "Rabbi Elazar opened and said, (Ecclesiastes 9:8) 'let your garments always be white, and let oil not be lacking on your head' - this verse has already been established, but come and see: the Holy One, blessed be He, created man in the secret of wisdom, made him with great craftsmanship, and breathed into his face a soul of life, to know and gaze upon the secrets of wisdom, to know the glory of his Master, as it is said (Isaiah 43:7) 'all that is called by My Name, and for My glory I have created it, I have formed it, I have even made it' - 'and for My glory I have created it,' precisely. And this secret we have learned: that the glory below, the secret of the holy Throne, is not established above except through the repair of the world's inhabitants, when those human beings are meritorious and pious and know how to make proper repairs - this is 'and for My glory I have created it' - for the sake of that glory, to establish it with mighty pillars and to adorn it with the adornment and ornament from below, so that this glory of Mine be raised through the honor of the righteous who are on earth; therefore 'I have created it,' along the lines of the supernal glory, whose repairs are within it" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:61: We find, then, that when the righteous man repairs his deeds in such a way that he is called by the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He - merciful, righteous, pious - the Shechinah, called "glory," is repaired; and the righteous man was created only for the repair of the Shechinah's glory, whose arousal depends on the repair done by the lower beings, as is explained in the Zohar (Bereishit 35a), on the verse (Genesis 2:6) "and a mist went up from the earth," etc., and likewise in the portion of Terumah (155b), in the explanation of the verse (Psalms 119:126) "it is time to act for the Lord": it says that when Israel occupies itself with Torah, that "time" of faith is repaired in its repairs and adorned in perfection as is fitting, and when Israel is idle from Torah, as it were, that "time" is not in its repair and is not found in perfection or in light - this is [the meaning of] "it is time to act for the Lord," etc. - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:62: This is the matter of "the Rock that bore you, you have weakened" (Deuteronomy 32:18), which is explained in the Zohar (Terumah, there), and which our Sages, of blessed memory, also explain (Eichah Rabbah 1:33), that Israel adds strength to the Gevurah above or weakens its strength, etc. We find, then, that one who performs Torah and mitzvot gives honor to his Maker, since all created beings do His honor and His will, and whoever does not perform mitzvot diminishes his Maker's honor.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:63: Likewise, it says in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu, quoted in the Yalkut at the beginning of Ezekiel (remez 340), on the verse "son of man" (Ezekiel 2:1) - his words: "son of upright men, son of righteous men, son of those who perform kindness, son of those who demean themselves for My honor and for the honor of Israel. Another interpretation: 'son of man' - to what can this be compared? To an earthly king whose wife and children rebelled against him; he arose and drove them from his house and cast them outside. In time, he sent and brought one son from her; he said to him, 'son of so-and-so, come, I will show you my house and my dwelling place besides your mother - has my honor and my Shechinah diminished at all, even though your mother stands outside?' Therefore he was compared to Ezekiel, son of Buzi the priest, as it is said (Ezekiel 1:1) 'and it came to pass in the thirtieth year,' etc. - this was the first year; but in the second, (ibid. 1:4) 'and I looked, and behold, a storm wind,' etc., 'and from within it the likeness of four Chayot' - after He showed him the whole Chariot, He said to him, 'son of so-and-so, this is My glory, and I have honored you above all the nations of the world - has My glory diminished at all, or the house I built [or: My Shechinah]?' As it is said (ibid. 43:11) 'and if they are ashamed,' etc. Lest you say, I have no one who serves Me - behold, I already have nine hundred and six myriad thousands of ministering angels who stand before Me and sanctify My great Name every day continually, from sunrise to sunset, saying, 'Holy, Holy, Holy,' and from sunset to sunrise saying, 'Blessed is the glory of the Lord from His place' - not to mention the seventy languages [nations] on earth. Why, then, do you do ugly things and unfitting things and rebel against sufferings? But I shall act for My Name's sake, that it not be profaned" - so far. Something close to this wording is brought at the end of Sefer Vayikra Rabbah (see 2:8), and from there I have corrected the wording and added a little to it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:64: The sixth aspect concerning honor is what the verse says (I Samuel 2:30) "for those who honor Me I will honor, and those who demean Me shall be treated with contempt"; and several aspects concerning this honor are explained in the Zohar and the Tikkunim: the first, concerning prayer, in which one must concentrate along the way of the secret - this matter Rashbi explains (Vayelech 285a), and we shall not quote all his words, since we need to explain the essence of this matter in the section on prayer - he says: "what is 'those who demean Me shall be treated with contempt'? This is one who does not know how to unify the holy Name and to bind the bond of faith and to draw down blessings to the place where they are needed and to honor his Master's Name; and whoever does not know how to honor his Master's Name, it would have been better for him not to have been created." Along these lines of this aspect is what Scripture says (Isaiah 29:13) "with his mouth and with his lips he honors Me, but his heart is far from Me" - they explain that the honor of the supernal attributes is through the illumination of the supernal soul, the soul for all the souls within them, and therefore when a person's mind cleaves to his heart's intent, he cleaves to the inner reality, and causes the thought to spread within the attributes, and through them the Infinite and the [supernal] Crown spread, and everything becomes a single unity; but if the heart is not there, matters are found like a body without a soul, like broken vessels with nothing inside them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:65: Further there (Vayelech 285a), Rabbi Yehudah said: "those who demean Me shall be treated with contempt" refers to whoever does not know how to honor his Master's Name and does not concentrate on "Amen," for we learn that greater is one who answers "Amen" than one who recites the blessing - so far, as relevant to us. And further on there: we learn, whoever hears a blessing from the one reciting it and does not concentrate on "Amen" for it, of him it is said "those who demean Me shall be treated with contempt," along the lines of (Malachi 1:6) "to you, priests, who demean My Name." And when he needs [mercy], what is his punishment? Just as he did not open blessings above, so they do not open for him; and not only this, but when he leaves this world, they proclaim before him and say, "lock the gates before so-and-so, let him not enter, do not receive him" - woe to him, woe to his soul - so far. And they further elaborate on the punishment of one who does not answer "Amen," further on there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:66: The practical rule that emerges from the totality of this passage is that, besides the plain meaning understood from his words - that one must concentrate on "Amen," whether the concentration is according to the plain sense, or along the secret way, which seems more apparent, as it says "just as he did not open blessings," etc. - one must be careful not to speak during the reader's repetition of the Eighteen Blessings, since these are blessings adjacent one to another, and if he speaks of his own affairs he will confuse his mind and be unable to concentrate on "Amen" even according to the plain sense; and likewise, in every single blessing among the other blessings, he should not converse from the beginning of the blessing to its end, so as to concentrate properly on "Amen." Besides this, one must be careful during the reader's repetition of the Eighteen Blessings, for this is a great blemish, as will be explained in the matter of prayer.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:67: Further, concerning "those who demean Me shall be treated with contempt," it is explained at the beginning of the portion of Va'etchanan (260b) that this refers to one who opens his eyes while praying - his words: "'those who demean Me shall be treated with contempt' - this is one who gazes at the Shechinah at the time he prays" - the rest of his words we quoted in the Gate of Holiness, at the end of chapter 8.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:68: In the midrash (Bemidbar Rabbah, Naso 8:3), on the verse "a man or a woman who commits any of the sins of man" (Numbers 5:6), it says concerning the verse "for those who honor Me I will honor" - his words: "another interpretation: 'for those who honor Me I will honor' - among converts, who honor the Holy One, blessed be He, by abandoning their evil deeds and coming to take shelter beneath the wings of the Shechinah, the Holy One, blessed be He, honors them - to teach you that whoever straightens his ways honors the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Psalms 50:23) 'whoever offers thanksgiving honors Me,' and it says (Jeremiah 13:16) 'give honor to the Lord your God before He causes darkness,' etc. And 'those who demean Me shall be treated with contempt' - these are the wicked, since they turn away from the Omnipresent, the Holy One, blessed be He, treats them with contempt" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:69: Further, concerning the honor of the Lord, even though the word "kavod" is not mentioned, is standing up to answer "Amen, may His great Name be blessed," etc., and "Barchu" - this is explained in the Jerusalem Talmud: "arise, for the Lord speaks to you" (see Judges 3:20) - from this Rabbi Elazar said, when they answer "Amen, may His great Name be blessed" and any matter of holiness, one must stand upon his feet - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:70: Further, concerning the honor of the Lord, is the warning to one who writes the Name, that he must concentrate on it properly, and Rashbi, peace be upon him, was very stringent about this in the portion of Acharei Mot (65b) - his words: "he said to him, Elazar my son, from now on be careful not to write the holy Name except properly, for whoever does not know how to write the holy Name properly and to bind the bond of faith, a bond of one with one, in order to unify the holy Name, of him it is written (Numbers 15:31) 'for he has despised the word of the Lord and has broken His commandment; that soul shall surely be cut off,' etc." - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:71: Further, concerning the honor of the Lord, is what Rashbi explains (Vayigash 207b), that whoever does not rise to occupy himself with Torah from midnight onward nullifies the honor of the Lord and is called "rebuked" - we shall quote his words below.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:72: Further, one must be careful not to speak mundane conversation in the synagogue, as they say in the portion of Terumah (131b), that whoever converses in the synagogue causes disrespect to the supernal arrangement above - we shall quote the rest of his words in their place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:73: Further, a seventh aspect concerning honor is what the verse says (Psalms 50:23) "whoever offers thanksgiving honors Me," and our Sages, of blessed memory, say (Sanhedrin 43b): Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, whoever sacrifices his inclination and confesses is as though he honored the Holy One, blessed be He, in two worlds, as it is said "whoever offers thanksgiving honors Me" - it is not written "yechabdeni" [honors Me, simple] but "yechabdaneni" [in an expanded form] - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:74: Further, an eighth aspect for practical purposes is what the prophet says (Isaiah 24:15) "therefore in the lights [urim], honor the Lord," and likewise it is said elsewhere (Judges 9:9) "and the olive tree said to them, should I stop my richness, with which they honor God and men?" And although this is said as a parable, no word is written in vain in the Prophets, but rather all certainly pertain to practical matters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:75: In the midrash we found support for this matter, quoted in the Yalkut, portion of Beha'alotcha (remez 719): "candles of flesh and blood, of clay or of copper - all according to a person's honor; and the honor of the Sabbath is its candles, which are its glory. If you kept the candles of the Sabbath, I shall show you the candles of Zion, as it is said (Zephaniah 1:12) 'at that time I will search Jerusalem with candles' - and I will not require you to see by the light of the sun, but rather I shall illuminate for you with My own glory, as it is said (Isaiah 60:19) 'the sun shall no longer be your light by day, nor for brightness shall the moon give light to you, but the Lord shall be to you an everlasting light' - and the nations are destined to walk by your light, as it is said (ibid. 60:3) 'and nations shall walk by your light.' And by what light does the Holy One, blessed be He, illuminate for Israel? By the light of righteousness, as it is said (Malachi 3:20) 'and the sun of righteousness shall rise for you who fear My Name.' And why all this? By the merit of the candles that they kindle on the Sabbath. Know how precious the commandment of the candles is before the Holy One, blessed be He, for even though the Holy One, blessed be He, does not need light, He commands Moses to warn Aaron (Numbers 8:2) 'speak to Aaron and say to him, when you light the candles'" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:76: At the end of his words there is also relevance to the candles we kindle in the synagogue, which corresponds to the Temple, as it says, "know how precious the commandment of the candles is before the Holy One, blessed be He, that He commands Moses," etc., and this applied to the Temple or the Tabernacle.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:77: Further, concerning the merit of the candles, in the midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 31:4) - their words: "another interpretation: 'command the children of Israel' (Leviticus 24:2) - Bar Kappara opened, 'for You shall light my candle' (Psalms 18:29). The Holy One, blessed be He, said to man: My candle is in your hand and your candle is in My hand. Your candle is in My hand, as it is said (Proverbs 20:27) 'the candle of the Lord is the soul of man'; My candle is in your hand, to light the perpetual candle. But the Holy One, blessed be He, said, if you light My candle, behold, I shall light your candle - hence, 'command the children of Israel'" - so far. Therefore it is fitting to light candles in the synagogue. Further, in the midrash (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:18), it says that Oved Edom was blessed because he honored the Ark, lighting one candle in the morning and one candle in the evening.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:78: Further, a ninth aspect concerning honor is found, and it is concerning charity. Solomon the king, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 14:31) "but whoever honors Him is gracious to the needy" - the reason being that the poor and the needy are her broken vessels, and the Shechinah dwells among them, as it says (Isaiah 57:15) "I dwell in the high and holy place, and with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit" - therefore whoever honors the poor with his money honors his Shechinah. We shall further elaborate on the matter of charity in the Gate dedicated to it, with the Lord's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:79: Further, a tenth aspect, concerning the honor of father and mother, in the Yalkut, portion of Va'etchanan (siman 830) - his words: "another interpretation: 'remember the Sabbath day' - 'honor your father and your mother' - what is the connection between these? Rather, to teach you that whoever honors his father and mother, no profanations of the Sabbath come to pass through him, as it is said (Isaiah 56:2) 'happy is the man,' etc. - do not read 'mechalelo' [who profanes it] but 'machul lo' [it is forgiven for him]. Let no one say, since my Father in Heaven preceded him first [in the honor due], I will do the will of my Father in Heaven and set aside the honor of my father and mother - whoever seeks days and wealth and possessions and honor and life in this world and the World to Come, and abundant life for the World to Come, let him do the will of his Father in Heaven and honor his father and mother. Another interpretation: 'honor your father' - Isaac fulfilled this, at the time he was laid before his father like a lamb to be led to slaughter. Another interpretation: 'honor your father' - Joseph fulfilled this, as it is said (Genesis 37:12) 'and Israel said to Joseph, are not your brothers pasturing in Shechem?'"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:80: Another interpretation: "honor your father" and "you shall not murder" - what is the connection between these? Rather, to teach you that if a person has the means and does not feed and support his father and mother, it is as though he murdered before the Omnipresent. Another interpretation: "honor your father" and "you shall not commit adultery" - to teach you that if a person has the means and does not honor his father and mother, it is as though he committed adultery before the Omnipresent. Another interpretation: "honor" and "you shall not steal" - if he does not do his father's and mother's will, it is as though he steals souls before the Omnipresent. Another interpretation: "honor" and "you shall not bear false witness" - whoever does not support his father and mother is as though he testifies falsely before the Omnipresent - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:81: In the Yalkut, portion of Vayigash (remez 152), on the verse (Genesis 46:1) "and Israel journeyed, and all that he had," etc. - his words: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, I went around to all the masters of aggadah in the south, that they might explain this verse to me, and they could not, until I came to Yehudah ben Padaya, the son of Bar Kappara's sister, and he said to me: when the teacher and the student walk on the road, they first ask after the peace of the student and afterward the peace of the teacher [an allusion to Jacob greeting his sons before God]. Rav Huna said, when Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi came to Tiberias, he asked Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish [about this]; Rabbi Yochanan said, a person is more obligated in the honor of his father than in the honor of his grandfather; Reish Lakish said, he offered [a sacrifice] concerning the covenant of the tribes - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:82: Further, one must be careful about the honor of elders, as it is said (Isaiah 24:23) "and before His elders, glory." And our Sages, of blessed memory, say in the Sifrei (Beha'alotcha, piska 34): not in one place, nor in two places, do you find that the Holy One, blessed be He, accords honor to elders, but rather everywhere - in the Sanhedrin, "gather to Me seventy men of the elders of Israel" (Numbers 11:16); similarly, "go and gather the elders of Israel" (Exodus 3:16); and to Moses He said, "come up to the Lord, you and Aaron, Nadav and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel" (ibid. 24:1); "and it came to pass on the eighth day that Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel" (Leviticus 9:1). Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says, from where do we know that even in the future to come He will accord honor to elders? As it is said (Isaiah 24:23) "and before His elders, glory" - it does not say "before His angels" or "before His prophets," but "before His elders." And so you find that the Holy One, blessed be He, grieves over a single elder as over all Israel, as it is said (ibid. 47:6) "I was angry with My people, I profaned My inheritance" - one might think it is profaned because of everything - the verse teaches, "upon the elder you have made your yoke very heavy." And is this not an argument from minor to major - if He who spoke and the world came into being is destined to accord honor to elders, how much more so must flesh and blood accord honor to elders - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:83: However, there is a dispute among the Tannaim (Kiddushin 32b) - some hold that any elderly person is meant, and some hold specifically an elder learned in Torah. And in the Yalkut (Ki Tisa, remez 393), on the verse (Exodus 33:7) "and it came to pass that everyone who sought the Lord went out to the Tent of Meeting" - this teaches that whoever sees the face of an elder is as though he received the face of the Shechinah - so far. It appears that this is said of an elder learned in Torah, since Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was an elder learned in Torah. This matter is likewise brought in the Yalkut (see Yalkut Shmuel, siman 96), on the verse (I Samuel 2:11) "and the boy Samuel ministered to the Lord before Eli the priest" - it appears specifically an elder learned in Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:84: In the midrash (Ruth Rabbah 6:2), they say concerning the verse (Ruth 3:10) "blessed are you of the Lord, my daughter" - their words: Rabbi Yochanan said, a person should never refrain from going to an elder that he may bless him. Boaz was eighty years old and had not been remembered [with children]; once that righteous woman prayed for him, he was remembered. Ruth was forty years old and had not been remembered; once that righteous man blessed her, she was remembered - "blessed are you of the Lord, my daughter" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:85: Just as we are commanded to honor the Torah and its students, so we must be careful not to honor the wicked, as it is said (Numbers 24:11) "I said I would greatly honor you, but behold, the Lord has withheld you from honor." Certainly Balak's words were not written in our Torah for naught, but for practical relevance, and further, the Name YHVH is mentioned among them, saying "the Lord has withheld you from honor." The reason is that what we are commanded to honor the students and elders of Torah is because the light of the Lord's glory flows into them, and whoever honors them honors YHVH; but the wicked, since he is removed from holiness, should not be honored - on the contrary, it is a mitzvah to hate him and demean him in order to subdue the kelipah, as David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 139:21) "do I not hate those who hate You, O Lord?" etc. Therefore one must be careful not to give greeting to a wicked man; and so Rashbi explains (Vaera 23b), on the verse (I Samuel 25:6) "peace be to you, and peace to your house" - they raised the difficulty: did David not know that Nabal was wicked, yet he preceded him with a greeting of peace and called him "living"? And they resolved that what David said, "you are peace," he said in reference to the Holy One, blessed be He, as is explained there, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "living," etc., and it says, from this we learn that it is forbidden to give a greeting of peace to a wicked person first, and if he must, let him give it as David did, blessing the Holy One, blessed be He, and let it be seen that he says it for His sake; and if you say this is deceit - it is not, for whoever elevates his intent to the Holy One, blessed be He, and it is seen that he says it for His sake, is not deceit; and whoever precedes a righteous person with a greeting of peace is as though he preceded the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself with it - so far. And what he says, "whoever elevates it to the Holy One, blessed be He," is similar to what our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Avodah Zarah 16b), that one says, "the judge is trustworthy to me" [as an oath by God, though it may not be recognized as such]. Concerning the punishment of flatterers, we shall elaborate in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 12, see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:86: Further, there is an eleventh aspect included in honor: to be careful of everything that involves demeaning His honor, blessed be He, or disgrace, for the opposite of honor is demeaning and disgrace, as it says (I Samuel 2:30) "for those who honor Me I will honor, and those who demean Me shall be treated with contempt."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:87: One must be careful of what Scripture says in the portion of Shelach Lecha (Numbers 15:31) "for he has despised the word of the Lord... that soul shall surely be cut off," etc., which our Sages, of blessed memory, explain in several ways, and one must be careful of all of them. They say in the passage "one who says the Torah is not from Heaven" (Sanhedrin 99a) - their words: our Rabbis taught, "for he has despised the word of the Lord" - this refers to one who says the Torah is not from Heaven. Another interpretation: this refers to a heretic [apikoros]. "And has broken His commandment" - this is one who breaks the covenant of circumcision. "That soul shall surely be cut off [hikaret tikaret]" - "cut off" in this world, "surely" [i.e., again] in the World to Come. From this Rabbi Elazar HaModa'i said: whoever profanes sacred things, and demeans the festivals, and breaks the covenant of our father Abraham, and shows a false face in Torah, not according to law, and shames his fellow publicly - even though he has Torah and good deeds like Moses our teacher, peace be upon him - has no share in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:88: It is taught elsewhere: "for he has despised the word of the Lord" - this refers to one who says the Torah is not from Heaven; and even if he says the whole Torah is from Heaven except for this one verse, which he claims Moses said on his own, not from the Holy One, blessed be He - this is "he has despised the word of the Lord." Even if he says the whole Torah is from Heaven except for this fine point, or this analogical inference [gezerah shavah] - this is "he has despised the word of the Lord." It is taught: Rabbi Meir used to say, whoever learns Torah and does not teach it to others - this is "he has despised the word of the Lord." Rabbi Natan says, whoever does not pay attention to the Mishnah [teachings]. Rabbi Nehorai says, whoever is able to occupy himself with Torah and does not. Rabbi Yishmael says, this refers to one who worships idols. What is the source that the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught this? That this refers to one who demeans the utterance the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke to Moses at Sinai, "I am the Lord"... "you shall have no other gods," etc. - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:89: Concerning the matter of "apikoros," they say there: Rav and Rabbi Chanina, both said, this refers to one who demeans Torah scholars. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi and Rabbi Yonatan say, this refers to one who demeans his fellow in the presence of a Torah scholar. And they say there, some teach it regarding the latter clause, "one who shows a false face in Torah, not according to law" - Rav and Rabbi Chanina say, this refers to one who demeans the face of a Torah scholar. Rabbi Yonatan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say, this refers to one who demeans his fellow's face in the presence of a Torah scholar. According to the one who says demeaning Torah scholars themselves is "showing a false face in Torah," this is consistent with saying that demeaning one's fellow in the presence of a Torah scholar is "apikoros." But according to the one who says demeaning one's fellow in the presence of a Torah scholar is "showing a false face in Torah," what would be "apikoros"? Rav Yosef said, one who says, "what benefit have the Rabbis given us? They have read for themselves, they have learned for themselves." Abaye said to him, is this "apikoros"? (In astonishment.) This is "showing a false face in Torah," for it is written (Jeremiah 33:25) "were it not for My covenant day and night," etc. (meaning, the sages sustain the world). Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said, you can learn this from here too (Genesis 18:26) "and I will forgive the whole place for their sake." But then who is [called] "apikoros"? Such as one who sits before his teacher and a teaching arises from another source (meaning, he recalls a halacha his teacher taught elsewhere), and he says, "we said thus there," and does not say, "the Master said thus there." Rava said, such as the house of Binyamin the physician, who say, "what benefit have the Rabbis given us? They never permitted us the raven or forbade us the dove" (meaning, they never said anything novel to permit the raven and forbid the dove). Rav Pappa said, such as one who says "these Rabbis" (meaning, this is a demeaning expression) - Rav Pappa himself once forgot and said "these Rabbis," and sat in a fast. Rav Nachman said, this refers to one who calls his teacher by his own name, as it is said (II Kings 8:5) "and Geichazi said, my lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life" [omitting the honorific] - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:90: Further, there is a twelfth aspect concerning honor, namely to honor one's Maker with praise and glorification, as it is said (Psalms 29:9) "and in His Temple all say Glory"; we have elaborated on this matter in the Gate of Love, in the matter of joy, for that is its proper place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:91: Concerning the whole aspect of honor we have explained, it says in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu, quoted in the midrash (Bemidbar Rabbah 5:9) - his words: Elijah says: they gathered and went out to war, and fifty thousand men fell of them, and the Great Sanhedrin fell with them; who killed them? You must say, none but the men of Beit Shemesh killed them, because they gazed at the Ark; and this is why He warned the sons of Kehat (Numbers 4:20) "and they shall not come in to see," etc. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: just as I did for the sons of Kehat, because they feared Me, I honored them and accorded them honor and warned concerning them to save their souls from death, so whoever fears Me, I honor him and do not cut off his name from the world. From whom do you learn this? From the sons of Yonadav ben Rechav, who, because they did My will - what is written of them? (Jeremiah 35:19) "a man of Yonadav ben Rechav's line shall not be cut off, standing before Me all the days." And if this is what I did for them, who are converts, how much more so for Israel, who are the children of My beloved, the children of My friend, when they do My will - they shall stand before Me all the days, as it is said (Isaiah 48:18) "had you but heeded My commandments, then your peace would have been like a river," etc., and it says (Deuteronomy 4:4) "but you who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:92: We saw fit, to complete this Gate, to explain the verses of fear found in the Torah, Prophets, and Writings, that pertain to practice.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:93: The first fear in the Torah, in the sin of Adam, the first man, is (Genesis 3:10) "and I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid." The matter is that Adam, the first man, before his sin, had a garment of light [ohr with an ayin], and after his sin, the supernal light was removed and stripped from him, and it became physical and clothed in garments of skin [ohr with an aleph]. This is [the meaning of] "and I was afraid" - he feared because he saw himself naked of the supernal light. So too every person must have this aspect of fear, that he not cause the light of the Shechinah to be removed from him through his sin, for through engaging in Torah and mitzvah a person draws the light of the Shechinah upon himself, and if, God forbid, he sins, it withdraws and he remains naked - this is another aspect concerning fear of sin besides what I have explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:94: The second: to be careful about the fear of the Name all day, as it is said (Proverbs 23:17) "but in the fear of the Lord all the day." And the pious Rabbeinu Yonah writes in his Iggeret HaTeshuvah that it is a great pillar concerning the Torah, that the fear of Heaven should not depart from before your eyes all the day, as it is said "but in the fear of the Lord all the day." And the plain sense of the verse we must say is thus: "let your heart not envy sinners" - whom should you envy instead? "But in the fear of the Lord" - in the merit of the fear of the Lord, saying, why am I not one who fears the Lord all the day? For sinners are those lacking completeness, along the lines of "and I and my son Solomon will be chata'im [deficient/sinners]" - "but in the fear of the Lord" - like those who have the fear of the Lord all the day; it appears that one must be God-fearing all the day. And what reminds a person of fear is that he wear tefillin all day, if possible, or at least during the hours he is occupied with Torah, when he is free from worldly affairs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:95: Let him learn that the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded the king (Deuteronomy 17:19) "and it shall be with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Lord," etc., and our Sages, of blessed memory, explain that a Torah scroll was always with him, and therefore he was constantly reminded of fear - this is [the meaning of] "that he may learn." Their words in the Tosefta (Sanhedrin 4:4): when he goes out to war, it is with him; when he enters, it is with him; when he sits at home, it is beside him; when he enters the bathhouse, it waits for him at the door. So too David says (Psalms 16:8) "I have set the Lord before me always," etc. Rabbi Yehudah says, the Torah scroll on his right and tefillin on his left. And it says further on there: if so, why is it said (Deuteronomy 17:18) "and he shall write for himself a copy of this Torah"? This teaches that he writes two Torah scrolls for himself, one that goes in and out with him, and one that is placed for him within the house; the one that goes in and out with him does not enter with him into the bathhouse or the privy, as it is said "and it shall be with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life" - in a place fit for reading it. And is this not an argument from minor to major - if the king of Israel, who was occupied only with public affairs, is said of him "and it shall be with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life," how much more so other human beings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:96: Along these lines (Deuteronomy 34:9) "and Joshua son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands upon him," etc., and so it says, "Joshua son of Nun, a young man" (Exodus 33:11), and so it says (Joshua 1:8) "this book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth, and you shall meditate on it day and night" - and is this not an argument from minor to major: if of Joshua son of Nun, who was occupied with conquering the Land and was about to divide it for Israel, it is said "shall not depart," etc., how much more so other human beings - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:97: Here we see that the king needed a Torah scroll with him, and according to Rabbi Yehudah, tefillin as well; and since it is not possible for a Torah scroll [to be constantly with everyone], which we were not commanded regarding, it is fitting to fulfill [the mitzvah of] tefillin - and therefore the earlier sages were careful about tefillin all day.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:98: Now, certainly what reminds a person of fear is engaging in Torah, since they said (Avot 2:5) "an ignoramus cannot fear sin" - from this you see how great an obligation rests upon us to occupy ourselves with Torah, from which fear is aroused, which is called the fear of the Lord, as it is said (Psalms 19:10) "the fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever"; and the whole reality of the Torah scroll and tefillin is to remind one to occupy himself with Torah constantly, as it is said (Exodus 13:9) "so that the Torah of the Lord may be in your mouth" - and this is "this book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth," as explained in the passage.
